name: Bremgarten faux Pre War
notes: Circuit Bremgarten, laid out through the forest north of Bern and opened in 1931 for motorcycles, with the first car race following in 1934. Seven kilometres of high-speed curves with no true straight anywhere on the lap, run clockwise under a canopy of trees that kept the surface patchily damp and the light shifting from bright to dark mid-corner — a combination that made it one of the most feared circuits in Europe. It held the Swiss Grand Prix from 1934 to 1939 and again from 1947 to 1954, until Switzerland banned circuit racing in the wake of the 1955 Le Mans disaster and ended its career for good. This is a pre-war dressing of the circuit.
author: Legion
